pairs.why: A's palm fills the frame on a dune ground like the real card; the camera angle is nearly the same in both, so the gap is small.
A has a mild, even top-face view and a calmer floor, while B's floor boards converge steeply and look wide-angle, which the real cards avoid.
B is tilted and seen in 3/4 view like the floating real objects, while A is a flat high-angle disc.
A's lean and the amount of cap top face match the real bottle slightly better, but both are close.
A shows the clock face-on, mounted on the striped wall with a soft wall shadow, like the real card. B puts it on a ground plane with a horizon, which the real card does not have.
The real card looks down from a high angle and shows a large table top. A shows more top face and ground than B, whose view is nearly edge-on and flattens the top.
A's truss spans the full frame width and the light hangs from it with a similar front-below view. B's truss is shorter and has stronger perspective.
A's slide fills the frame and its tile ground plane sits low and close, like the real card. B pulls back and adds more depth between hero and pool.
